latest_release.name: TensorFold 1.3.3
latest_release.body:
# TensorFold 1.3.3

1.3.3 makes GLM faster. On CUDA, GLM-5.3-Flash drafted decode after a 1,040,384-token prompt is 13.8% faster at TP=4. On Macs without tensor units, GLM cold prompts take 5.17% to 5.68% less time. It adds picture generation for MOSS-Image on CUDA through `POST /v1/images/generations`, GLM-OCR on HIP, DFlash2 drafting for GLM-5.3-Flash on Metal, EXL3 `mcg` experts at 1 to 8 bits for GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA, structured output for DeepSeek-V4.1 on CUDA, and Idol's image encoder on Metal. The server gains an opt-in execution witness, a prompt-cache flush route, per-request deadlines (`deadline_s`), structural tags, deferred and namespace tools, and `TENSORFOLD_PARALLEL`. By default, long prompts on CUDA now share their steps with running replies, each image takes a fixed share of the visual-token budget, and LFM2-MoE, LFM3, MiniMax-M3 and Qwen3.5-2B on Metal fill new prompts between other streams' decode rounds. The speed changes below keep the same tokens, bits or bytes where their bullets say so.

## Speed

- **GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA (long-context decode):** drafted decode after a 1,040,384-token prompt takes its DSA index scores from `tf_glm_index_scores`. It is 13.8% faster at TP=4 (172.39 against 151.51 tok/s median), with byte-identical scores and the same tokens. Shorter windows keep `tf_glm_scores` (#3689).
- **GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA (TP=3, 5, 6 or 7):** at these widths a rank's fused KDA input is not a multiple of eight columns. The stack is now padded at load to its own width rounded up to eight columns and stays row-major bf16, so prompt windows take the staged B16 tiles with every byte as before. `TF_GLM_KDA_PAD=1` still tiles the stack for `glm_mm` (#3697, for #3516).
- **GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA (split drafter):** `TF_GLM_DRAFT_SPLIT=1` splits the DFlash2 drafter's MLP across three ranks or more where each share is 256-aligned, without `TF_ROCE=1`. The ranks must set it alike, two ranks split as before, and unset changes nothing. On three GB10s whose gathers stay on NCCL, decode with `--drafter` is about 5% faster at one stream (four streams within their start-to-start spread), with the same replies and the same tokens a round on the measured prompts. As with `TF_ROCE=1`, the split drafter adds its down projection's rank shares in another order, so its proposals can differ at near-ties (#3616, for #3581).
- **GLM on Metal before M5 (prompts):** vectorized prompt, KDA and indexer kernels on Macs without tensor units cut cold prompt time 5.17% to 5.68% (2K to 64K tokens), with 0/64 token differences. (#3921, refs #3152).
- **GLM on Metal (DFlash2):** decoding skips inactive draft rows and their tap capture, and the tap mean writes into its ring in place. This cuts sampling overhead without changing verified tokens (#4257).
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 on Metal (multi-stream decode):** a decode round over several streams runs each per-stream stage (window key, compressed rows and index keys, ratio-2 pooling, decode attention, index scores, candidate blocks and the top 512) as one dispatch over a table of the streams' state. There is one barrier between stages instead of one a stream, and the bits are the same (#2954, refs #2984).
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 on Metal (sampling and drafts):** DSpark drafts are selected over the whole vocabulary on the GPU with an adaptive block size (#3405). Sampling keeps its scratch between picks and scans greedy logits in vectors, choosing the same IDs (#3288).
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 on CUDA (copy drafter):** opt-in `TF_DSV41_COPY_DRAFTER=1` turns on the lookup planner with a copy drafter that ranks matches within a length band by how much continuation they offer. It offers 8 drafts, widens to 15 after a round that keeps every copy, and offers a copy only when it is expected to keep at least as many tokens as the other drafter. It is refused when `TF_DSV41_LOOKUP` is off or blank, and unset leaves `TF_DSV41_LOOKUP_PLAN=1` as it was (#2638).
- **Flash Next on CUDA (draft head):** a bf16 language head

Help Support TensorFold · @tensorfold_dev on X

# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-with-agents). ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, a small 4-bit checkpoint. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). The [run guide](docs/run-guide.md#platform-setup) lists the archive's requirements; Windows has [its own guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). ```sh V=1.3.4 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. To talk to a model in the terminal in one command, `tensorfold chat MODEL` starts the server itself, streams each reply and stops the server when the chat ends; `/help` lists the chat's commands, and `/bye` or Ctrl-D ends it: ```sh tensorfold chat mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit ``` With the server above still running, `tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` chats with it instead, and `echo "Say hello." | tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` prints one reply for a script. See [the chat command](docs/chat.md) for its flags and the serve flags it passes on. ## Docs - [Run guide](docs/run-guide.md): platform setup, requests, parallel requests, exact decoding, context compaction, Cortheon mode, every serve flag, the Mac app and TensorFold Starlight. - [Supported models](docs/supported-models.md): which checkpoints run on which machines, models on disk and model discovery. - [Living Weights (experimental)](docs/living-weights.md): teach a running model new facts in its own weights. - [Installation runbook](RUNBOOK.md): macOS and CUDA installation, paired Metal serving and troubleshooting. - [Windows](docs/WINDOWS.md), [TensorFold Web](docs/web.md) and [the Mac app](app/README.md). - [API](docs/api.md), [Cortheon mode](docs/cortheon.md) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) and [community benchmarks](docs/community-benchmarks.md). - [Usable memory profiles](docs/memory-profiling.md): how to record applied budgets, context, cache state and process peaks. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): ATC and agents, builds, tests and the exactness and performance gates. - [Changes](CHANGELOG.md), [1.0.0 release notes](docs/release-notes-1.0.0.md) and [the Zig engine preview](docs/zig-preview.md). - TensorFold is Apache-2.0: [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE),
